strengths: Principled framework that addresses the fidelity-horizon trade-off by decoupling global narrative modeling (mean-seeking flow matching) from local dynamic realism (mode-seeking reverse-KL distillation).
Enables efficient few-step (4-step) long video generation at inference time using the distribution matching head without multi-stage pipelines.
Comprehensive empirical validation across multiple metrics, user studies, and comparison against both SFT and autoregressive baselines.
weaknesses: Training requires significant computational overhead due to simultaneous long-sequence flow matching, on-policy student rollouts, and VAE decode/re-encode operations for boundary alignment.
Limited sensitivity analysis regarding key hyperparameters, particularly the balancing weight lambda_seg between the two conflicting objectives.
Qualitative results still exhibit challenges with fine-grained temporal compositionality and non-cyclic event planning over long horizons.

strengths: Sound conceptual framework decoupling mean-seeking global temporal structure (via SFT flow matching) from mode-seeking local fidelity (via sliding-window distribution matching).
Effective dual-head architecture sharing an encoder to mitigate gradient interference between contrasting optimization objectives.
Enables fast, few-step (4 NFE) generation at test time while maintaining high dynamic degree and visual fidelity compared to standard SFT and autoregressive baselines.
weaknesses: Empirical validation is primarily conducted on 30-second clips, leaving the claimed generalization to minute-scale or multi-minute sequences largely under-tested.
